game: Kent State Golden Flashes@Ohio State Buckeyes

guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our numbers see the mismatch in both directions. Kent State has struggled to create value on the ground or consistently reach scoring territory, while Ohio State grades among the strongest defenses in both areas. That combination creates the possibility of short Kent State possessions and repeated favorable field position for Ohio State.

We also see considerable continuity on the other side. Ohio State returned eight offensive starters, including Julian Sayin, who completed 77.0 percent of his passes in 2025. The 671-yard performance against Ball State provides an early example of that offense producing through both the passing and running games, though we are not treating one result as proof of what follows.

The issue for us is the price rather than the matchup. Ohio State replaced eight defensive starters from last season, and the market is already demanding an extreme margin. Our expectation is only slightly more favorable to Ohio State, leaving too little separation from the market once the sensitivity of such a large spread is considered. That is why we pass.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
For us, Kent State's rushing offense against Ohio State's run defense is the matchup that best explains the potential game script. Ohio State held Ball State to 45 rushing yards in the opener, and our broader rankings show an even larger underlying advantage for the defense. If Kent State cannot generate efficient early-down runs, sustaining drives becomes difficult and Ohio State gets more chances to create separation.

That does not automatically make the favorite valuable. The market is already pricing a highly one-sided game, so this matchup supports the blowout case without creating enough disagreement for us to bet it.

recent_game.fact: Ohio State opened the 2026 season with a 56-3 win over Ball State on Sept. 5.
Against Ball State, Ohio State produced 671 total yards, including 434 passing and 237 rushing, while allowing 165 total yards.
Ohio State held Ball State to 45 rushing yards, 120 passing yards and a 21.4 percent third-down conversion rate.
Fourteen Ohio State players recorded a reception against Ball State, the program's first game with at least 14 receivers making a catch since Sept. 22, 2018.
Wide receiver Jeremiah Smith caught eight passes for 151 yards and two touchdowns in the first half against Ball State.
Running back Bo Jackson averaged 9.2 yards per carry against Ball State and scored on a career-long 65-yard run.
Ohio State played 21 true freshmen in the opener, and freshman Legend Bey had 100 all-purpose yards and scored on his first career reception.

quarterback.fact: Julian Sayin returns as Ohio State's starting quarterback after starting 15 of his first 19 career games.
Sayin completed 77.0 percent of his passes for 3,610 yards, 32 touchdowns and eight interceptions in 2025.
Sayin's 77.0 percent completion rate in 2025 set Ohio State and Big Ten single-season records.
Justyn Martin is the only other quarterback listed with prior game experience, having appeared in six games without a start.

offensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returns eight offensive starters: quarterback Julian Sayin, running back Bo Jackson, wide receivers Jeremiah Smith and Brandon Inniss, tackle Phillip Daniels, center Carson Hinzman, and guards Luke Montgomery and Austin Siereveld.
Ohio State lost three offensive starters from 2025: guard Tegra Tshabola and tight ends Max Klare and Will Kacmarek.
Ohio State's starting offensive line had combined for 146 games played and 93 starts after the season opener.
Ohio State returned 85.8 percent of its offensive-line snaps among players who logged at least 100 snaps in 2025.
Center Carson Hinzman entered the season with 36 career starts, while Austin Siereveld had 21 and Phillip Daniels and Luke Montgomery each had 17.
Wide receiver Devin McCuin transferred from UTSA after recording 65 receptions for 726 yards and eight touchdowns in 2025.
Wide receiver Kyle Parker transferred from LSU with 34 career receptions for 385 yards and five touchdowns.
Bo Jackson rushed for a team-high 1,090 yards on 179 carries as a freshman in 2025.

defensive_personnel.fact: Ohio State returns three defensive starters: cornerback Jermaine Mathews Jr., defensive end Kenyatta Jackson Jr. and safety Jaylen McClain.

Ohio State lost eight defensive starters from 2025: tackles Tywone Malone Jr. and Kayden McDonald, end Caden Curry, linebackers Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles, safeties Caleb Downs and Lorenzo Styles, and cornerback Devin Igbinosun.
Defensive tackle James Smith and defensive end Qua Russaw transferred to Ohio State from Alabama.
Defensive tackle John Walker transferred from UCF after totaling 64 tackles, eight tackles for loss and 1.5 sacks in 26 career games.
Linebacker Christian Alliegro transferred from Wisconsin with 127 career tackles and eight sacks.
Safety Earl Little Jr. transferred from Florida State after leading that team with 76 tackles in 2025.
Kenyatta Jackson Jr. recorded 11 tackles for loss and 6.5 sacks in 2025.
Jaylen McClain was Ohio State's sixth-leading tackler with 53 tackles while playing 816 defensive snaps in 2025.

coaching_changes.fact: Ohio State's 2026 coordinators are defensive coordinator Matt Patricia, offensive coordinator Arthur Smith and special teams coordinator Robby Discher.
Tyler Bowen is Ohio State's run game coordinator and offensive line coach, while Billy Fessler is the pass game coordinator and quarterbacks coach.

offensive_context.fact: Through the opener, Ohio State averaged 56.0 points, 671 total yards, 434 passing yards and 237 rushing yards per game.
Ohio State converted 45.5 percent of its third downs and scored on every red-zone possession in the opener.
Since Ryan Day became head coach in 2019, Ohio State has averaged 39.6 points per game and has scored at least 50 points 23 times.
Since entering college football in 2024, Jeremiah Smith has recorded 171 receptions for 2,709 yards and 29 receiving touchdowns.

defensive_context.fact: Ohio State allowed 3.0 points and 165 total yards in its 2026 opener.
Ohio State allowed no red-zone scores in the opener and recorded seven tackles for loss, one sack and one interception.
Ohio State led the FBS in 2025 in scoring defense at 9.3 points allowed per game, total defense at 219.1 yards and passing defense at 129.7 yards.
Since the start of the 2024 season, Ohio State has allowed 37 touchdowns in 31 games and has held nine opponents without a touchdown.

special_teams.fact: Punter Joe McGuire is Ohio State's returning specialist starter.
Ohio State lost starting kicker Jayden Fielding and long snapper John Ferlmann from the 2025 team.

other_relevant.fact: Ohio State's schedule lists a home game against Kent State on Sept. 19, 2026, with a noon kickoff.
Ohio State entered the week after the Ball State game with a 1-0 record and the No. 1 Associated Press ranking.
